subject: Request: penetration assessment report + remediation timeline
messages:
From: Tom Keller <tkeller@phoenixretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@phoenixretail.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Request for penetration assessment report and remediation details

Jonas,

Following the anomalous activity we observed on our account last week, our security team is requesting a copy of Redwood's most recent internal penetration assessment (full report) along with a remediation tracker that lists findings, owners, and status. Phoenix Retail requires the report to decide whether to expand a temporary mitigation we put in place.

Specifically we need:
- Full penetration assessment report (redactions permitted for third-party IP)
- A remediation timeline and status for all critical/high findings from the report
- Confirmation of whether the incident we saw correlates to any item in the PT findings

We appreciate that some material will need to be redacted. Please indicate the process and expected turnaround, and whether we need to sign any supplemental NDA or go through an escrow access workflow. We are treating this as high priority and would like an initial response within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Tom Keller
Security Operations Manager
Phoenix Retail
[signature block]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tkeller@phoenixretail.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@phoenixretail.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration assessment report and remediation details

Tom —

Thanks for flagging this and sorry to hear about the anomalous activity. We take these requests seriously. Quick summary of our process and next steps: 

1) Scope & redaction: We can provide a redacted copy of our most recent penetration assessment. Redactions typically remove internal test harnesses and third-party contact details. For particularly sensitive artifacts we offer a limited "escrow view" (watermarked PDF, screen-shared review, or secure Drive access) under an access agreement.

2) Timeline: I can deliver an initial redacted summary and remediation tracker within 48 hours. Full escrow access or a less-redacted copy generally takes 3–5 business days due to legal and engineering review.

3) Correlation check: If you share the incident ID or timestamps you observed, our incident team will triage against the PT findings and provide a correlation statement.

4) Paperwork: We'll need a signed access attestation (routine) for any less-redacted disclosure. If you prefer, we can use an existing mutual NDA; otherwise I will attach a short access attestation for e-signature.

Attachments I will share in the initial reply: a high-level redacted summary (PDF) and a remediation tracker spreadsheet stub. If that looks good, I will escalate to Vanessa for approval to provide escrow access.

Proposed immediate next step: Please reply with the incident ID(s) or sample timestamps and confirm whether Phoenix can accept a redacted PDF + tracker first, or if you require escrow access upfront.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_summary_redacted_v1.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)]
[attachment: remediation_tracker_stub.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)]
From: Tom Keller <tkeller@phoenixretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@phoenixretail.com>, Legal <legal@phoenixretail.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration assessment report and remediation details

Jonas —

Thanks, that timeline is reasonable. Incident ID is PHX-20270408-77. Timestamps: 2027-04-08 02:13:22 UTC and 2027-04-08 02:17:40 UTC.

We'd accept the redacted PDF + tracker first and reserve the right to request escrow access if our triage suggests a closer match. Legal is looped in to confirm if they need a separate attestation. We appreciate a 48-hour turnaround.

Tom

On a related note: given the customer-facing nature of the data affected, our executive team may request an exception to our data retention clause if the report indicates additional exposure. I'll flag that if it becomes necessary.
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tkeller@phoenixretail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@phoenixretail.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration assessment report and remediation details

Tom, Jonas —

I'm looping in to approve the redaction + share path. We will: 
- Share a redacted PDF (redwood_pen_test_summary_v1.pdf) that removes internal tool output and tester IDs.
- Attach a remediation tracker (redaction_plan_v1.xlsx) showing severity, owner, current status, and ETA.
- Provide correlation note from our incident team referencing PHX-20270408-77.

Please expect the redacted PDF and tracker in a secure Drive folder (link below) within 24–36 hours. For escrow or less-redacted access we'll require a signed access attestation; I will send the attestation template if Legal needs it.

Drive folder (secure, view-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPhx-PT-evidence
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/phoenix-retail

Attachments: [attachment: redwood_pen_test_summary_v1.pdf (PDF, 3.2MB)] [attachment: redaction_plan_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]

Jonas — please coordinate delivery and let me know if engineering needs additional context to speed up the redaction.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
